syntheticDisclosure.statement: All 13 regions, 12 portals, 3 frames, route geometry, portal closure state, entity observations, and team reports in this record are synthetic design data. They are not surveyed Korail facility geometry and are not operational procedure acceptance.
limits: DATA: All entity placements, roles, teams, frames, and portal closures are synthetic design inputs.
DATA: Negative observation tests assert confidentiality of synthetic incident data before discovery, not physical security verification.

CAPABILITY: The executed run is NOT NUnit and NOT the Unity Test Runner. It compiles the test file with the Unity-bundled Roslyn csc.dll plus the .NET 6.0.21 runtime against verbatim copies of the production sources, and runs the [Test] methods under a console runner and a local NUnit-shaped assertion shim. It therefore cannot show [OneTimeSetUp]/[SetUp] lifecycle, the Unity editor environment, test categories, NUnit3 XML, asset import, or PlayMode. A green run here shows the assertions hold against the production sources; it does NOT show the same tests pass inside the editor.

CAPABILITY: Two production files under test (Multiplayer/Runtime/NetworkFieldRuntime.cs, Multiplayer/Runtime/ConnectedWorldRuntime.cs) are MonoBehaviours that depend on Unity.Netcode/Unity.Collections/UnityEngine, for which no assembly exists outside the Unity project Library. Their projection methods are compiled from verbatim line-range copies, not from their compiled assemblies. The copied blocks and their per-block sha256 are listed under runRecord.executedRun.extractionManifest; if production diverges from a copied range, that block's digest stops matching and the run must be re-taken.

COVERAGE GAP: No UI render surface is exercised by this record, so the UI branch of acceptance criterion 2 is NOT shown false here. A UI render surface DOES exist inside the audited production file: NetworkFieldRuntime.cs:1116 declares OnGUI, and it renders exactly the strings that criterion is about - routeDisplay.RouteLabels and routeDisplay.UnavailableReason at lines 1135-1136, and routeDisplay.ProcedureHint at line 1140. The test file constructs no MonoBehaviour and can never enter OnGUI, and the harness compiles the projection methods as line-range copies rather than running the component, so no UI code path is reached. An earlier revision of this entry asserted that no UI surface existed in the unit at all; that was false as written, because the surface exists and is simply untested. The 'four surfaces' named in the acceptance criteria are realised here as three exercised surfaces - authoritative server state, the client observed view, and the route/guidance projection - plus a negative command-submission surface.

COVERAGE GAP: A stale FRAME mismatch and a stale REPORT mismatch are NOT exercised. The mismatch test covers a stale entity revision (CommandCode.StaleTarget), a non-existent report target (CommandCode.UnknownTarget) and an out-of-reach target (CommandCode.OutOfReach). A frame that has moved since the client read its snapshot is not constructed, and neither is a stale report snapshot. acceptance_3 is narrowed to the three rejection paths that are actually executed.

COVERAGE GAP: Mutation probe M14 SURVIVES the repaired suite. M14 forces ProcedureHintsVisible on at NetworkFieldRuntime.cs:1001 even in Evaluation mode; no test in this file moves with that behaviour. The mode-scoped visibility rule is owned by issue #138's FMP-11b scope, not by this unit, and is declared here rather than claimed covered.

COVERAGE GAP: Several production branches are never reached by any test in this file, so a mutation applied to them would be a no-op and was not filed as a surviving mutant: Occluded, TargetBlocked, RoleDenied, IdentityMismatch, WrongWorld, AuthorityBusy, CommandIdConflict, canOperate and the Evaluation mode branch. Their absence from mutation results is a coverage hole, not evidence that they are correct.

COVERAGE GAP: The SnapshotFreshness half of the acceptance-4 test duplicates coverage already held by the existing SnapshotFreshness test suite. It is retained here only as the second term of a separability assertion and is not offered as new freshness coverage.
COVERAGE GAP: Mutation probing targeted the projection surfaces and the named rejection codes. It is not an exhaustive mutation of every branch in the two extracted files.

The rewrite preserved every tree EXACTLY, so no file content changed and no digest was invalidated by it -- only the commit identities moved. That rebase left another set of revisions this record had bound reachable from no ref -- the run taken at fe34d40487de36540be98b805bd5ac9e49fc3b54 (tree 41b87679af57cb2c6007f3f8dabc7aab1be31d73), now unreachable from any ref. The tip immediately before this rebase was 52cd5ca -- it is the commit entry the reflog places directly before the rebase-start entry -- and fe34d404 was already orphaned by the FIRST rebase, being the parent of the fixup commit 6f8b9b1 and not an ancestor of that rebase's output f68dfe6; and the record commits 4b1fe2f, 0a236bc, f68dfe6, 15c0c13 and ddec511..52cd5ca, whose post-rebase counterparts are c93764f, 8419770, e45f9c4, 31f55db and 8d56715..7c9b1c9. The FIRST rewrite preserved every tree exactly, and its mapping pairs show it by direct tree comparison: a7ff7d8d -> 42e2488, both tree cf037ed6eb2a14c0; 578c024f -> 3c873cf, both tree 663549fdee24b3fc. issueTestCases.name: PortalConsistencyMatchesAuthoritativeResponseAcrossAllSurfaces
issueTestCases.surfaceScope: Portal: Active door -> Portal Open -> Route available vs Inactive door -> Portal Closed -> Route blocked unavailable; plus actor-region scoping of ProjectPortals and exclusion of a portal the visibility delegate rejects

issueTestCases.name: FrameConsistencyMatchesAuthoritativeResponseAcrossAllSurfaces
issueTestCases.surfaceScope: Frame: Local-to-world Point3 translation (the origin, the two authored yaw 0 frames this file reads, and a constructed yaw 90 frame) -> Moving frame displacement -> Route CrossesFrame boundary projection. The yaw 90 frame is deliberately not from the authored profile: every authored frame has sin(yaw) = 0, so no authored frame pins the SINE term of the transform, and that term is what this constructed frame exists to pin. The profile's third frame (train-metro, yaw 180) is NOT read by this file and is not covered here; it does separate a rotation-applying transform from a rotation-ignoring one, through cos(180) = -1, and that case is pinned by Fmp08aMovingFrameTests.cs in the same test assembly, not by this unit. An earlier revision of this entry listed the yaw 180 frame as covered and justified the yaw 90 frame with the stronger claim that the profile cannot distinguish the two transform classes at all; both were wrong and are corrected here.

issueTestCases.name: ReportConsistencyMatchesAuthoritativeResponseAcrossAllSurfaces
issueTestCases.surfaceScope: Report: Submit report -> Teammate observed report reception -> Cross-team isolation (read) -> Teammate acknowledge -> Cross-team acknowledgement rejection

executedRun.attemptsNote: The field counts DISTINCT sourceRevision.describe values the driver recorded for this bundle -- one per revision it was run at, not one per invocation. That definition is deliberate, because a per-invocation count is not recoverable: runs overwritten in place left no artefact, and several directories hold more than one run-record.json at the SAME describe (a probe, a refuter, a baseline-only run), so counting directories would overcount while counting deliverables would undercount. Re-derive the field by collecting the describe values from the run directories and counting the distinct ones; there are ten. THREE were taken against dirty trees and none of them is bound here: 70f5163-dirty, e45acca-dirty, and f35781a-dirty -- the last taken after the driver's M14 note had been corrected but before that correction was committed, and discarded for exactly that reason. SIX were taken on clean, committed trees and were later superseded, either by a rebase or by this rebind: 79a6e22, fe34d40, f68dfe6, 15c0c13, 7c9b1c9 and f35781a. One of the six recorded 162 accumulated extraction-manifest entries because the manifest was not reset between cases, which inflated run-record.json to 47735 bytes; the reset was fixed and the driver re-run, and disk byte-consumption rather than a test outcome was the reason for that fix. Another corrected the four reporting defects described in reRunNote. The run at fe34d40 was left reachable from no ref by the second rebase, which is why this note exists at all; the run at 7c9b1c9 was the previous binding. The TENTH is the run recorded here, 4ca07e0, and it is the one this record binds. This is a count of revisions run at, not a census of every document that exists: directories from three other bundles also carry a run-record.json, and they are excluded because their testFileSha256 is a different, pre-hardening test file. An earlier revision of this note understated the run count relative to this field, and separately claimed the recorded run was the first taken on a clean tree that carried the hardening; both were false and are corrected rather than narrowed. What is true of the recorded run is what sourceRevision.dirtyCompiledPaths states: the tree was clean across every compiled path.
executedRun.reRunNote: The driver was run a fourth time to correct four reporting defects found by an adversarial audit of this bundle. (1) The unmutated baseline was labelled 'survived', which filed a passing control under mutant-escape vocabulary and inflated the survivor count; it is now 'baseline_passed' and the survivor list holds M14 alone. (2) The scope note did not disclose that the harness compiles exactly ONE test file, which is the actual reason M14 survives here. (3) The record bound no source revision, and 27 of the 30 compiled files carried no digest at all. (4) The mutation spec's own note said 7 tests where the file declares 8. The driver and the spec were edited, and run-record.json was REGENERATED -- the recorded run was not edited after the fact. driverSha256, runRecordJsonSha256, mutationSpecSha256 and runRecordJsonSizeBytes above were re-read from the regenerated files. rawOutputSha256 is UNCHANGED: the test outcomes are deterministic, so the raw log is byte-identical across the two runs, which is itself evidence that the edit changed the reporting and not the measurement. All six extractionManifest block digests are unchanged. The verdicts are otherwise identical (27 cases, 25 caught). collectedAt above is the filesystem mtime of the regenerated run-record.json, because the driver emits no timestamp of its own. The runs recorded here were taken with --out pointing outside the repository and the two artefacts were then copied in, for exactly that reason. One further re-run followed the hardening edits: because the test file changed, run-record.json was regenerated and rawOutputSha256 moved with it. The raw log does NOT carry a source revision: its header records the compiler, the runtime, the worktree token, the test file path and the test file's sha256, and nothing else. What it echoes is that test-file CONTENT digest, so a carried-over log could not have matched once the test file changed; the digest moving is the check that the artefacts belong to this run. An earlier revision of this note said the log echoed the source revision, which would have sent a verifier looking in the log for a revision that is not there. The mechanism is corrected here; the conclusion it supported still holds, on the content digest. mutationSpecSha256 was UNCHANGED by that re-run, since the spec was already final. || 2026-09-16, after an adversarial audit of the hardening wave: a later re-run corrected the spec notes, the test file's yaw-90 axis prose and one leak assertion, so BOTH mutationSpecSha256 and rawOutputSha256 moved with it, and the run was re-taken at the rebased tip rather than carried over. Its verdicts are unchanged: 28 cases, 26 caught, M14 the only survivor, baseline passing.
executedRun.extractionManifestNote: These six entries are the manifest exactly as produced by the recorded run (run-record.json, extractionManifest, 6 entries). The sha256 values here were read back from that file, and the manifest's own sha256 for each block remains authoritative: recompute from run-record.json rather than trusting this copy. If a copied block ever diverges from production, its digest stops matching.

mutations.survivedNote: run-record.json reports status 'survived' for exactly one case, 'M14'. The unmutated control is reported as 'baseline_passed' and excluded from the survivor list, because a run with no mutant applied cannot escape one. M14's survival is a limit of this harness rather than evidence that no test pins the guard: M14 forces ProcedureHintsVisible on in Evaluation mode (NetworkFieldRuntime.cs:1001), and FMP11bModeResponseTests.cs in the same test assembly asserts ProcedureHintsVisible ten times. What M14 falsifies is the Evaluation-mode suppression, pinned at five sites (lines 254, 260, 287, 328, 360); the other five are the Practice-mode positive (lines 227, 234, 288, 327, 354), which still passes under M14. Only the five Evaluation sites would fail, so citing the Practice sites as pinning evidence would overstate that file's coverage of this guard. None of the ten is compiled here either, since this harness compiles only the one FMP-11c test file. The extractionScopeNote inside run-record.json states both scope limits.

baselineControl.note: Unmutated control. The status is 'baseline_passed', not 'survived': a case with no mutant applied has nothing to escape, and filing it under mutant-escape vocabulary inflated the survivor count by one in an earlier revision of this record.

mutations.method: Each mutation is a single-defect production edit applied to the scratch copy of the production sources before compilation; a mutation is CAUGHT when at least one assertion in the test file fails or errors, and SURVIVED when all tests still pass.

runRecord.reRunNote: The driver writes run-record.json and harness-raw-output.txt into its own directory by default. Re-running it there OVERWRITES the committed artefact and makes the digests recorded above stop matching. To re-run without clobbering the recorded evidence, pass --out <a different directory>. runRecord.artefactFidelityNote: harness-raw-output.txt records the worktree it ran in as the token <WORKTREE> in place of an absolute path, so the file carries no operator home directory, no session directory and no account name.
